cohort: A total of 1137 women aged 19-45 who had singleton and live births and complete medical records were included.
finding: Elevated prepregnancy BMI and inappropriate gestational weight gain are significantly associated with increased risks of various adverse maternal and neonatal health outcomes including gestational diabetes, macrosomia, cesarean delivery, low APGAR scores, low birth weight, and prolonged neonatal hospitalization.
mod_finding: Overweight and obese women had significantly higher odds of elective cesarean delivery.
followup_time: Up to and beyond 5 days post-birth for neonatal hospitalization.
